paragraphs.text: A byte-budget gate for agents on metered proxies: direct-first, stall-triggered proxy, hard per-call
/per-day caps, per-hop redirect checks, local ledger. Cross-platform (macOS/Linux/Windows). DeepSeek
Harness plugin + standalone CLI.
# dsh-traffic-guard

A **byte-budget gate for metered proxies** for DeepSeek Harness (dsh).
Agent downloads go direct by

default; the local proxy is used only when a direct attempt actually stalls,
and every proxied byte
is charged against a hard per-call / per-day budget and written to a local ledger.

One CLI (`netguard`, usable standalone) + one Host plugin exposing three tools:
`net_usage`, `net_pr
obe`, `net_download`.
> 中文: README.zh.md
## Why
When your egress is metered (a paid proxy plan, a mobile hotspot, a corporate gateway), **traffic is

money**.
Agents make that easy to lose:

- a single `curl -O`, `git clone` or `pip install` can be hundreds of MB;
- desktop apps' **nightly

auto-updaters** download full bundles in the background — we measured a single
**347.7 MB** update,

and its updater used Chromium's network stack, which **honours the system proxy**,
so it really did

spend plan traffic;
- proxy clients usually report only an account-level total, **with no per-app or

per-host attribution**;
- meanwhile CLI children (curl/git/npm) often ignore the system proxy, so "

some traffic goes through the
proxy and some doesn't" and the accounting never lines up.
`dsh-traffic-guard` turns this into one auditable policy: **direct first → escalate only on stall →
hard budget → everything logged**.
## What it does
| Layer | Behaviour |
| **Routing** | Direct by default. Only hosts in `proxy_hosts` may use the proxy, and only after a d
irect attempt fails / returns zero bytes / reads too slowly. The proxy is discovered from the OS (`s

cutil --proxy` on macOS, `NETGUARD_HTTP_PROXY` elsewhere); no hardcoded port. |
| **Budget** | Proxi
ed calls are capped per call (default 128 MiB) and per day (default 300 MiB). Exceeding either is a

hard failure (exit 3); only `--force` overrides. Direct traffic is free and not charged. |
| **Redir
ects** | Automatic following is disabled and **every hop is re-evaluated** (borrowed from SSRF-guard

plugins): a redirect from a proxy host to a direct host is re-decided, not blindly proxied. |
| **P
re-checks** | If `Content-Length` already exceeds the call budget, nothing is downloaded; while stre

aming, bytes are counted and the read is aborted on overflow. |
| **Timeouts** | One `max_time` budg

et for the whole redirect chain, so N hops cannot multiply the wait. |
| **Ledger** | One JSONL row
per call: timestamp, URL, host, route, bytes, duration, outcome, matched rule. `report` aggregates b

y day and host. |
| **Fail cache** | A host that recently failed direct repeatedly skips the direct
attempt next time, saving the 8 s stall each call. |
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

or install the checkout as a local bundle with `plugin_manager` (`action: install_bundle`,
`target:

<absolute path to this repository>`). The plugin has no dsh dependencies (Node builtins only),
so a
linked package works.
Tools exposed to the model: `net_usage`, `net_probe`, `net_download`.
## Portability: other machines, other proxy clients
**It is not tied to one proxy vendor.** Neither the plugin nor the CLI contains vendor-specific code

;
`dsh-traffic-guard` only needs a local **HTTP/HTTPS proxy** and a metered plan. Any client that ex

poses an
HTTP proxy port works — Clash/mihomo, Surge, Stash, sing-box, V2Ray, a corporate egress gat

eway, or an SSH
tunnel bridged to HTTP. The optional `status` line that reads a local client's `/sta

tus` endpoint is a
nicety: when no such endpoint exists it is simply skipped.
The author's client-side split-routing rules are **not** part of this repository — routing policy in

side a
closed-source client is a different problem, and no vendor formats or keys are shipped here.
### How the proxy address is discovered
| Priority | Source | Notes |

| 1 | `config.proxy.url` | e.g. `"http://127.0.0.1:7890"` — most explicit, works everywhere |
| 2 |

`NETGUARD_HTTP_PROXY` env | Same format; good for CI and per-shell overrides |
| 3 | OS detection |
macOS `scutil --proxy`; Windows WinINET registry; GNOME `gsettings` |
SOCKS-only clients are not supported by Python's `urllib`; use the client's HTTP proxy port (most cl

ients
expose one) or a local HTTP→SOCKS bridge.
### What a migration needs
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- The ledger (`~/.dsh/netguard/ledger.jsonl`) is **per machine**; copy it along if you want history

to continue.
- Budgets are enforced by `netguard` only; the OS and the proxy client still apply thei

r own limits.
- Auto-detection is best-effort: the Windows/Linux detectors are implemented, but CI o

nly exercises the
deterministic config/env paths. Set `config.proxy.url` when in doubt.
## Standalone CLI

Exit codes: `0` ok, `3` budget/size refused, `4` network failure, `5` proxy needed but unavailable.
## Configuration

`$NETGUARD_HOME/config.json` (default `~/.dsh/netguard/config.json`); see
cli/config.example.json.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`proxy_hosts` are hosts **allowed** to use the proxy when direct stalls (not "must use proxy").
`dir
ect_hosts` are hosts that **never** use the proxy and take precedence.
## Compared with related dsh plugins
The ecosystem already has egress-security plugins; this one is about **budget and accounting**:
| Project | Focus | What we borrowed |
[该节后续省略]
## Limitations
- **Not an OS-level firewall.** It constrains downloads that go through `netguard`. Bypassing calls
(`curl`, `git clone`, app auto-updaters) are not stopped, though they show up in system/plan totals.
- Proxy clients generally have **no per-app attribution**; this plugin fills that gap with its own

ledger,
which only covers calls routed through it.
- The budget is a hard constraint on the agent, n

ot on the machine: `--force` overrides it, and other
processes can still use the same proxy.
- HTTP/

HTTPS proxies only (urllib has no SOCKS support); use the client's HTTP proxy port.
- Proxy discover

y: macOS `scutil --proxy`; Linux/Windows via `NETGUARD_HTTP_PROXY`.
- Contains no vendor-specific co
nfiguration formats or keys.
